title: Silent Failure Rate
description: A metric for how often an automation platform accepts a unit of work, reports no problem, and does not complete it.

definitions.missed: The platform accepted the event and nothing arrived at the destination.
definitions.partial: The platform accepted the event and some, but not all, of the expected effects arrived.

denominator.definition: Runs the platform accepted AND that the workload expected to produce output. Runs correctly stopped by a filter are excluded and reported separately.

exclusions.definition: The platform refused the event at the moment of delivery: a non-2xx status, a timeout, or a connection failure. No run was created.
exclusions.rationale: The sender learns immediately and can retry. This is the opposite property from the one the metric measures. Combining them yields a number that cannot distinguish a loud, recoverable failure from a hidden, unrecoverable one.
exclusions.note: This is the load-bearing rule of the metric.

exclusions.definition: Events fired by an edge probe (destination outage, success-wrapped failure, sustained load).
exclusions.rationale: A stress test must not share a denominator with normal operation, or the headline rate stops describing normal operation.

interval.rationale: Zero failures in 40 runs and zero in 4,000 are different claims. Publishing both as 0% misleads by omission.

workloads.expected_receipts: 1 per poll finding a new item, 0 for an empty poll

conformance.claim_applies_to: a published measurement, not an organisation
conformance.partial_claim_rule: If a requirement is not met, claim the level below and state what is missing.

levels.name: Reported
levels.summary: An SFR computed from your own operational data and reported so it can be evaluated.

levels.name: Measured
levels.summary: A controlled measurement rather than an observation of your own traffic.

levels.name: Stress
levels.summary: L2 plus the three edge behaviours ordinary operation never exercises.
levels.note: Each probe must be published including when its result is that nothing interesting happened.

event.run_id: unique per event, preserved unchanged to the destination

send_outcome.note: Recording that a send failed without recording why makes connection reset, timeout and non-2xx indistinguishable, and the distinction is unrecoverable after the fact.

latency.note: Not the platform's internal execution time; do not compare with a figure that is.
